description: Delegated supervision: event streams -> challengeStatuses (packages/shared/src/investigation/supervision.ts). The Cardinal plugin's Python mirror runs the same cases. expected: every challenge.added of the stream, by seq, -> {status, ruling_seq, owner_seq, correction_seq, verification_seq}; correction_seq is correctionOf(challenge) (the worker's current correction) for addressed / directive_addressed and the verdict statuses, else null, so the fixture pins correctionOf too. The derivation's display-only `verdicts` list is not part of this contract. Events carry the wire fields the derivation reads (seq, type, class, payload, producer.is_investigation_author, authority on owner.decided: only owner_decision overrules, and on verdicts producer.lineage_root_id when present, else producer.principal.id, as their grant lineage: grt_…002 with lineage_root_id grt_…001 is grt_…001's successor; grt_…003 is another lineage). Version 3 (cardinal-agent-plugins docs/specs/supervision-verdicts.md, revision 5): verification.recorded verdicts, correctionOf, and supersedes_verdict (only active verdicts combine; a superseded one still judged k, and #<v> answers only a verdict on the current correction, before its revision). Cases may carry expected_next: by challenge seq, {actor: worker | supervisor | owner | nobody, action_kind: take_position | comply | submit_correction | verify_correction | rule | decide_conflict | reverify | decide_unverifiable | none} — nextAction(status, the deciding verdict's staleness) (§3, Next action); compared only where present.
